arguments.quote: TOML can be read with tomllib, which is in the standard library from Python 3.11, and pyproject.toml is where Python tools keep settings now.
arguments.text: TOML can be read with tomllib, which is in the standard library from Python 3.11, and pyproject.toml is where Python tools keep settings now

arguments.quote: We still support Python 3.9 and 3.10, where tomllib does not exist.
arguments.text: We still support Python 3.9 and 3.10, where tomllib does not exist

alternatives.status_quote: Decision: we will read a [tool.quillfmt] table from pyproject.toml using tomllib, with tomli on older Pythons. YAML is rejected because of the implicit typing surprises and the extra dependency. INI is rejected because it cannot express nested overrides.
alternatives.title: TOML inside pyproject.toml

arguments.quote: YAML please. Everyone already knows it from CI configs, and it reads nicely.
arguments.text: YAML please. Everyone already knows it from CI configs, and it reads nicely

arguments.quote: YAML worries me. Its implicit typing means a value like no silently becomes false, and we would need PyYAML as a new runtime dependency.
arguments.text: YAML worries me. Its implicit typing means a value like no silently becomes false, and we would need PyYAML as a new runtime dependency

arguments.quote: Fair, but a safe loader avoids the worst problems, and PyYAML is everywhere anyway.
arguments.text: Fair, but a safe loader avoids the worst problems, and PyYAML is everywhere anyway

alternatives.status_quote: YAML is rejected because of the implicit typing surprises and the extra dependency
alternatives.title: YAML file

arguments.quote: INI through configparser is in the standard library, so it costs zero dependencies.
arguments.text: INI through configparser is in the standard library, so it costs zero dependencies

arguments.quote: INI cannot express nested tables or lists cleanly. Our per-language overrides need nesting, so INI would force awkward dotted keys.
arguments.text: INI cannot express nested tables or lists cleanly. Our per-language overrides need nesting, so INI would force awkward dotted keys

alternatives.status_quote: INI is rejected because it cannot express nested overrides
alternatives.title: INI file

arguments.quote: Executing user Python just to read configuration is a security risk when quillfmt runs in CI on untrusted pull requests. I am against it.
arguments.text: Executing user Python just to read configuration is a security risk when quillfmt runs in CI on untrusted pull requests

alternatives.description: Using a plain Python file for dynamic configuration
alternatives.status_quote: You're right about CI. I withdraw the Python config file idea.
alternatives.title: Plain Python file

arguments.quote: Could we also support a standalone .quillfmt.toml file for repositories that are not Python projects?
arguments.text: Could we also support a standalone .quillfmt.toml file for repositories that are not Python projects?

alternatives.description: Supporting a standalone TOML file for non-Python projects
alternatives.status_quote: Good idea, but let's postpone the standalone .quillfmt.toml file until after 1.0, because it needs its own file discovery rules.
alternatives.title: Standalone .quillfmt.toml file

arguments.quote: Separately, should we accept JSON configuration too? I could go either way.
arguments.text: Should we accept JSON configuration too? I could go either way

arguments.quote: JSON has no comments, which is painful for configuration files people edit by hand.
arguments.text: JSON has no comments, which is painful for configuration files people edit by hand

arguments.quote: True, although JSON5 would fix that. I have no strong opinion.
arguments.text: True, although JSON5 would fix that. I have no strong opinion

arguments.quote: Environment overrides would be handy in CI.
arguments.text: Environment overrides would be handy in CI

arguments.quote: Environment overrides would be handy in CI. +1 from me.
